candidates.original_title: Comparison of self-reported and device-based measured physical activity using measures of stability, reliability, and validity in adults and children
candidates.description: Investigating the stability of pairwise differences between accelerometry, diary, and questionnaire for measuring physical activity, and assessing reliability and validity of these tools in adults and children.
candidates.citation_sentence: the current study aimed to replicate the results of our previous study using data from the first SMARTFAMILY trial [8] with data from the SMARTFAMILY2.0 trial.
candidates.notes: Self-replication with mixed results: accelerometry findings largely replicated but diary/questionnaire findings partially reversed; authors state results 'reinforce' previous findings but note important differences and reversed roles of diary vs questionnaire.

candidates.original_title: Comparison of self-reported and device-based measured physical activity using measures of stability, reliability, and validity in adults and children
candidates.description: The original study examined the stability, test-retest reliability, and validity of physical activity estimates obtained using accelerometry with 10- and 60-second epochs, a physical activity diary, and a questionnaire in adults and children.
candidates.citation_sentence: Therefore, the current study aimed to replicate the results of our previous study using data from the first SMARTFAMILY trial [8] with data from the SMARTFAMILY2.0 trial.
candidates.notes: The paper explicitly describes the study as a replication and states that the present results reinforce the findings and conclusions of the original study. The questionnaire and diary procedures were intentionally modified, so this is coded as a close experiment rather than a direct replication. The citation uses numbered references rather than author-year format.
